summary: Request guidance to isolate burst budgets for mixed realtime and background ingest to mitigate 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer is seeing recurring 429 responses during daytime ingest windows when a background bulk ingest job overlaps with realtime chat traffic. Impact: Production latency spikes and client-side retry storms; customer reports 30-40% of realtime requests receive 429 over a 45-minute window. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-west serving both realtime (low-latency chat) and background ingest (bulk embedding pipeline).

Observed behavior: Realtime API calls intermittently return 429s with Retry-After headers. Throttles correlate with the dedicated pool's burst window being drained by concurrent background jobs. Expected behavior: Background ingest should not exhaust burst credits needed for latency-sensitive realtime traffic; guidance requested on configuration to isolate or reserve burst budget for realtime routes.

Request: Best-practice configuration steps (console + API), recommended burst pool weights/refill intervals for mixed workloads, and suggested rollout steps to avoid regressions. Customer also asks whether a conservative canary or traffic-splitting strategy is supported to test changes incrementally.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a high-concurrency background ingest (multipart bulk embed) against the customer's dedicated endpoint for 90+ concurrent workers
2) Simultaneously generate parallel realtime chat traffic from the product frontend (50-100 qps, short sessions)
3) Observe 429 responses on realtime endpoints after ~10-20 minutes when background ingest sustains high throughput
4) Check console -> Rate Limits panel and token/burst metrics for the dedicated pool during the window
5) Reproduce consistently by scheduling background job to overlap with peak frontend traffic window
logs: Sample client log: "received 429s from realtime endpoint for 37% of calls between 18:12-18:57"
comments: Support (Priya): Logged on behalf of DataWave Labs — they need a configuration approach to prevent background ingest from draining realtime burst credits in their dedicated pool.

Customer (DataWave Ops): We've observed this pattern after enabling a nightly bulk backfill that now runs during US peak hours. We can reschedule but want isolation without losing throughput for the background job.

SRE (Ethan): Requested telemetry — ask customer to provide 1 minute granularity charts around 'burst_credit_remaining', 'token_refill_rate', and 'concurrent_sessions' for the pool. Also asked for background job job-IDs and approximate per-worker rps.
Customer: Provided worker-count=96, avg request size ~2k tokens, background job id=backfill-20260314-01. Will attach time-aligned logs once available.

SRE: Noted this looks like classic burst pool contention. Proposed short-term mitigation: create a route-level isolated burst pool for realtime routes and set a smaller shared pool for background ingest. Asked to confirm ability to apply route config on dedicated tenant.
Support: Shared step-by-step draft will be posted as a follow-up comment once SRE confirms exact API flags to change.
investigation_notes: Checked dedicated-pool metrics: burst_credit_remaining trending to zero during overlaps; refill interval set to 60s, pool weight 1.0 for all routes.

Hypothesis: Background ingest jobs consume burst credits because route weight is equalized; token accounting treats both streams similarly causing realtime latency-sensitive traffic to be rejected when credits deplete.

Config investigation: Route-level 'burst_pool' and 'rate_priority' flags exist on dedicated pools API. There is also 'reserve_percent' for priority lanes but not exposed in console by default for dedicated tier; needs support intervention or documented API call.

Edge case noted: if we create isolated burst pool and background ingest is still allowed to borrow from shared pool (soft borrow), may still see transient 429s — need to ensure strict isolation (hard pool separation) or set borrow_threshold to 0.
Related internal: INT-4310 created to enable 'reserve_percent' in console for dedicated tenants and to add a safe rollback path for pool changes.
recommendations: Short-term (no code deploy): Use dedicated API to create a new isolated burst pool and map the realtime route(s) to that pool. Set 'borrow_threshold' to 0 for strict isolation and 'refill_interval' to 30s for realtime pool.
Medium-term: Configure 'reserve_percent' = 20% for realtime lane if strict separation not possible; set 'background' lane weight to 0.5 to reduce consumption during peak windows.

Rolling change advice: Apply config to one edge/route at a time and monitor '429 rate' and 'p50 latency' for 15-minute windows. Have fallback plan to revert mapping if errors rise in background ingest.
Client-side guidance: Implement exponential backoff with jitter and honor Retry-After. For realtime clients, use low-retry strategy to avoid retry storms (max 1 retry, jitter 100-400ms).
Operational follow-up: Schedule a 2-hour maintenance window to apply route mapping in production if customer prefers an outage-window for quick rollback.
resolution_notes: Provided API snippets and console steps to create an isolated burst pool and map routes: (1) POST /admin/pools with 'hard_isolate': true, 'refill_interval': 30; (2) PATCH /admin/routes/{route_id} { 'burst_pool': '<new-pool-id>' }.

Customer applied an isolated realtime pool in staging during a controlled test — realtime 429s dropped from ~37% to <2% during a 30-minute overlap while background ingest throughput remained ~85% of previous level.
SRE created INT-4310 to expose 'reserve_percent' and pool borrowing controls in the console for next sprint and to add telemetry alerts for 'burst_credit_remaining < 10% for >5m'.

Follow-ups: Customer requested assistance scheduling prod cutover next week. Recommend support SRE on-call during the window. Ticket marked for next-step coordination and will be closed after prod validation.
